    Python for non-programmers

    2. 02Try it yourself

    0 of 3

    Ready when you are.

    Only completion is saved on this browser. Never your notes or personal details.

    A small lesson. A useful new perspective.

    Start with the question, not the chart

    Choose a visual that answers one specific question.

    01 / Explore

    The idea, in practice.

    “What changed?” suggests a time series. “Which is largest?” suggests a sorted bar chart. Name the comparison before you choose the visual, and label the units directly.

    02 / Make

    A ten-minute experiment.

    Write one question your data should answer. Sketch the simplest chart that can answer it. Add a clear title and units.

    03 / Reflect

    A quick check-in.

    You want to compare the size of five categories. What is a useful first choice?

    A small step. A real start.

    You completed the sample lesson. Keep the question, try another draft, or explore the full curriculum.
